Lambda Check

Source: R/lambda_check.R
lambda_check.Rd

Verify if lambda functions are written with the shorthand \(x) (like \(x) x * 2). Return table message of the line with problems and a corrected version of the submitted function.

Usage

lambda_check(
  x,
  export = FALSE,
  out_path = ".",
  safer_check = TRUE,
  lib_path = NULL,
  error_text = ""
)

Arguments

x

A function name, written without quotes and brackets.

export

Single logical value. Write the corrected function into a file instead of returning it? If TRUE, the file <function name>_safer.R is written in out_path (e.g., fun_safer.R for x = fun). Nothing is returned or exported if nothing has to be corrected. An error is returned if exported and the file already exists.

out_path

Single character string indicating the path of the folder where to write the file when export = TRUE. "." (default) means the R working directory. Ignored if export = FALSE.

safer_check

Single logical value. Perform some "safer" checks? If TRUE, checkings are performed before main code running (see the safer-r project): 1) correct lib_path argument value 2) required functions and related packages effectively present in local R libraries and 3) R classical operators (like "<-") not overwritten by another package because of the R scope. Must be set to FALSE if this function is used inside another "safer" function to avoid pointless multiple checkings.

lib_path

Vector of characters specifying the absolute pathways of the directories containing the required packages for the function, if not in the default directories. Useful when R packages are not installed in the default directories because of lack of admin rights. More precisely, lib_path is passed through the new argument of .libPaths() so that the new library paths are unique(c(new, .Library.site, .Library)). Warning: .libPaths() is restored to the initial paths, after function execution. Ignored if NULL (default) or if the safer_check argument is FALSE: only the pathways specified by the current .libPaths() are used for package calling.

error_text

Single character string used to add information in error messages returned by the function, notably if the function is inside other functions, which is practical for debugging. Example: error_text = " INSIDE <PACKAGE_1>::<FUNCTION_1> INSIDE <PACKAGE_2>::<FUNCTION_2>.". If NULL, converted into "".

Value

A table-like message is always printed, with one row per reported lambda (column 1: line number; column 2: symbol; column 3: code before the lambda), or a message saying that everything seems fine.

If export = FALSE: the corrected function, or NULL if nothing has to be corrected.

If export = TRUE: NULL, returned invisibly. The corrected function is written in a file (see the export argument).

Details

Warning: the \(x) writing of a lambda function is only kept in the code of the submitted function when the function carries its source references (attribute srcref, e.g., after a base::parse(keep.source = TRUE) or a function defined in a file loaded with keep.source = TRUE). Otherwise, R prints the lambda as function(x), so that nothing can be reported: run lambda_check() on the source code itself, not on a compiled or on a loaded package function. The base::getOption("keep.source") default is TRUE in interactive sessions and FALSE in Rscript.

Reported: lambdas written \(x), like \(x) x * 2, \(x){ x } or \() base::mean(1:3), wherever they are written in the submitted function (right side of an assignment, argument value of a function call, etc.). In the message table, the SYMBOL column shows the lambda writing with its formals only when they are written on a single line: for a lambda whose formals span several lines, the fallback writing \() is shown (the whole writing is still replaced correctly in the code, because only the \ token is replaced).

Not reported: the function(x) standard writing, and lambda writings of the past (e.g., function(x) x) reported by other functions. Strings, comments and backquoted names (like a backquoted backslash, the deprecated function() writing of R versions before 4.1.0) are ignored: a backslash followed by ( inside a string, a raw string, a comment or a backquoted name is never reported nor modified, whatever the rest of the written text (the detection is token-based, not text-based). A lambda body itself is not modified: run curly_bracket_check() and true_false_check() afterwards to check the corrected function further.

Correction: each reported \ lambda writing is replaced by function (e.g., \(x) x * 2 becomes function(x) x * 2). The rest of the code is unchanged. The corrected code is checked by parsing it. Lines can become longer than 80 characters. The returned function keeps the environment of the submitted function.

Warning: the comments of the submitted function are lost in the returned function (its code is re-parsed). They are kept in the exported file, which contains the recovered code verbatim, only modified by the \ -> function replacements.

Line numbers are indicative. They start at the <- function line (#' header lines not counted). Compiled functions, like saferDev::colons_check, have no comments: their line numbers differ from their source file.

Author

Gael Millot

Examples

# Warning: these examples may not work well when using the "Run examples" link
# because of a particular environment. Please, copy-paste in a local environment.
# See also https://safer-r.github.io/saferDev/articles/lambda_check.html
# The \(x) writing is only kept in a function carrying its source references,
# hence the parse(keep.source = TRUE) writing used here:
code1 <- "function(x){ base::sapply(X = 1:3, FUN = function(y){ y * 2 }) }"
fun1 <- eval(parse(text = code1, keep.source = TRUE))
saferDev::lambda_check(fun1) # everything fine: NULL returned
#> 
#> 
#> AFTER RUNNING saferDev::lambda_check().
#> INSIDE fun1(), EVERYTHING SEEMS CLEAN.
#> 
#> NULL
code2 <- "function(x){ base::sapply(X = 1:3, FUN = \\(y){ y * 2 }) }"
fun2 <- eval(parse(text = code2, keep.source = TRUE))
fun2_safer <- saferDev::lambda_check(fun2) # lambda writing reported
#> 
#> 
#> 
#> INSIDE fun2(), SOME LAMBDA FUNCTIONS ARE NOT WRITTEN function():
#> 
#> LINE	SYMBOL		CODE
#> 1	\(y)		function(x){ base::sapply(X = 1:3, FUN = \(y){ y * 2 }) }
#> 
#> MODIFIED FUNCTION RETURNED BY return().
#> 
fun2_safer # corrected function
#> function (x) 
#> {
#>     base::sapply(X = 1:3, FUN = function(y) {
#>         y * 2
#>     })
#> }
#> <environment: 0x55a05dcf6820>
# A backslash followed by ( in a string, a raw string, a comment or a backquoted name
# is not a lambda writing (token-based detection): not reported, not modified.
code3 <- paste0(
    "function(x){ y <- \"the text \\\\(x) is inside a string\" ; ",
    "z <- r\"(raw \\(x))\" ; # a \\(x) in a comment\n    base::`\\\\`(x) ; x }"
)
fun3 <- eval(parse(text = code3, keep.source = TRUE))
saferDev::lambda_check(fun3) # everything fine: NULL returned
#> 
#> 
#> AFTER RUNNING saferDev::lambda_check().
#> INSIDE fun3(), EVERYTHING SEEMS CLEAN.
#> 
#> NULL
# Write the corrected function in the fun2_safer.R file of a new temporary folder:
tempo_dir <- base::tempfile(pattern = "dir", tmpdir = base::tempdir(), fileext = "")
base::dir.create(path = tempo_dir, showWarnings = TRUE, recursive = FALSE, mode = "0777")
saferDev::lambda_check(x = fun2, export = TRUE, out_path = tempo_dir)
#> 
#> 
#> 
#> INSIDE fun2(), SOME LAMBDA FUNCTIONS ARE NOT WRITTEN function():
#> 
#> LINE	SYMBOL		CODE
#> 1	\(y)		function(x){ base::sapply(X = 1:3, FUN = \(y){ y * 2 }) }
#> 
#> MODIFIED CODE EXPORTED IN:
#> /tmp/RtmpT24sDl/dir16a02d0efe87/fun2_safer.R
#>
